hook.text: WWII planes returned with bullet holes in the wings. The military reinforced the wings. Abraham Wald said: wrong.

buildup.text: The planes that didn't return had holes in the engines. Reinforcing wings was studying survivors, not victims.

discovery.text: Survivorship bias: we see what survived and ignore what didn't, drawing wrong conclusions from the visible.

twist.text: Business advice from billionaires ignores the millions who did the same things and still failed.

climax.text: To think clearly, always ask: what am I not seeing? Who dropped out? What data is missing?

punchline.text: The dead can't tell you why they didn't survive.

quiz.question: What is survivorship bias?
options: Drawing conclusions only from what survived, ignoring failures
